verses: إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقُونَ قَالُوا۟ نَشْهَدُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
ٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَهُمْ جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُمْ سَآءَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ءَامَنُوا۟ ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا۟ فَطُبِعَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ

وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ أَجْسَامُهُمْ وَإِن يَقُولُوا۟ تَسْمَعْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُّسَنَّدَةٌ يَحْسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيْحَةٍ عَلَيْهِمْ هُمُ ٱلْعَدُوُّ فَٱحْذَرْهُمْ قَٰتَلَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ
وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا۟ يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ لَوَّوْا۟ رُءُوسَهُمْ وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ وَهُم مُّسْتَكْبِرُونَ
سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ لَن يَغْفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لَا تُنفِقُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَنْ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ حَتَّىٰ يَنفَضُّوا۟ وَلِلَّهِ خَزَآئِنُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ
يَقُولُونَ لَئِن رَّجَعْنَآ إِلَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ لَيُخْرِجَنَّ ٱلْأَعَزُّ مِنْهَا ٱلْأَذَلَّ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تُلْهِكُمْ أَمْوَٰلُكُمْ وَلَآ أَوْلَٰدُكُمْ عَن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرُونَ
وَأَنفِقُوا۟ مِن مَّا رَزَقْنَٰكُم مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِىَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلَآ أَخَّرْتَنِىٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهَا وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys ↔ Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 opposite ruling.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 7.3). Pair score 14.7.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king; Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward); A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts]; Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die'; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant; At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won.

Only in Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay: Spend before death comes and one says 'My Lord, if only you would delay me a little, I would give charity'; God delays no soul when its term comes; It is the same whether the prophet asks forgiveness for the hypocrites or not; God will not forgive them; The hypocrites testify 'You are God's messenger'; God knows he is, and testifies that the hypocrites are liars; The hypocrites say 'When we return to Medina the mightier will expel the meaner from it'; but might belongs to God, his messenger and the believers; Let not your wealth and children divert you from God's remembrance; The hypocrites' bodies impress and their speech is heard, but they are like propped-up timbers, thinking every cry is against them; The hypocrites take their oaths as a shield (junna) and will swear falsely even to God at the resurrection; When you eat and are full, beware lest you forget God; God forbids the prophet to pray or intercede for the people, for he will not hear; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes; God opens his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain.

Only in Return to me; will a man rob God? Test me with the tithe: 'I YHWH do not change; therefore you sons of Jacob are not consumed'; 'Will a man rob God? Yet you rob me' in tithes and offerings; God opens the windows or gates of heaven, for blessing or for the flood [contrast between the texts]; 'Return to me and I will return to you', says God; Bring the whole tithe to the storehouse and test God: he will open the windows of heaven and pour out blessing without limit; Disputation form: God states a claim, the people object 'How have you...?', and God answers; Had they observed the Torah and Gospel they would have eaten from above them and beneath their feet; The tithe given to the Levites; Levites give a tithe of the tithe; The way (sunna) of God with those who passed before: you will find no change in God's way; Locust, worm and cricket devour crops, vines and trees.

Only in Al-Munafiqun: false testimony, propped-up timbers, 'the mightier will expel the meaner', and the deathbed plea for delay: Spend before death comes and one says 'My Lord, if only you would delay me a little, I would give charity'; God delays no soul when its term comes; It is the same whether the prophet asks forgiveness for the hypocrites or not; God will not forgive them; The hypocrites testify 'You are God's messenger'; God knows he is, and testifies that the hypocrites are liars; The hypocrites say 'When we return to Medina the mightier will expel the meaner from it'; but might belongs to God, his messenger and the believers; Let not your wealth and children divert you from God's remembrance; The hypocrites' bodies impress and their speech is heard, but they are like propped-up timbers, thinking every cry is against them; The hypocrites take their oaths as a shield (junna) and will swear falsely even to God at the resurrection; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life; In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts]; When you eat and are full, beware lest you forget God; God forbids the prophet to pray or intercede for the people, for he will not hear; God sets a seal on the unbelievers' hearts and hearing and a covering over their eyes.
